issues.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML — XSS risk if HTML comes from user data
issues.ai_explanation: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on line 352 bypasses React's XSS protection by directly setting raw HTML. If the `__html` value includes user content, attackers can inject malicious scripts.
issues.suggested_fix:
Sanitize with DOMPurify: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(content) }}`
Or render user content as plain text via JSX children.

issues.message: Math.random() for security-sensitive value — not cryptographically secure
issues.ai_explanation: `Math.random()` on line 23 uses a pseudo-random number generator that is predictable. Attackers can reproduce the sequence if they know the seed — dangerous for tokens, salts, and IDs.
issues.suggested_fix: Use `crypto.randomUUID()` for unique IDs or `crypto.getRandomValues()` for random bytes in browsers. In Node.js: `require('crypto').randomBytes(32)`.

issues.message: No USER instruction — container runs as root by default
issues.ai_explanation: Without a `USER` instruction, Docker runs the container process as root. If the application is compromised, the attacker has root access inside the container.
issues.suggested_fix:
Add before CMD/ENTRYPOINT:
`RUN groupadd -r appuser && useradd -r -g appuser appuser
USER appuser`
issues.after_code:
# Add near the end of your Dockerfile:
  RUN useradd -r -u 1001 -g root appuser
  USER appuser

issues.message: CORS wildcard origin (*) — any website can make credentialed requests
issues.ai_explanation: `*` as the allowed CORS origin on line 15 permits any website to read responses from your API, including with cookies/credentials if credentials are also enabled.
issues.suggested_fix: List specific allowed origins: `allowed_origins: ['https://yourapp.com', 'https://staging.yourapp.com']`

issues.message: No HEALTHCHECK instruction — container orchestrators cannot detect unhealthy state
issues.ai_explanation: Without `HEALTHCHECK`, Docker and Kubernetes cannot tell if the container is actually serving traffic. A locked-up process won't be restarted automatically.
issues.suggested_fix: Add: `HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s CMD curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1`

issues.message: Missing 'set -u' — unset variables silently expand to empty string
issues.ai_explanation: Without `set -u`, referencing an unset variable produces an empty string instead of an error. This can cause commands like `rm -rf $DIR/*` to become catastrophically destructive.
issues.suggested_fix: Add `set -u` (or `set -euo pipefail`) near the top of the script.

issues.suggested_fix: Use `crypto.randomUUID()` for unique IDs or `crypto.getRandomValues()` for random bytes in browsers. In Node.js: `require('crypto').randomBytes(32)`.

issues.message: No USER instruction — container runs as root by default
issues.ai_explanation: Without a `USER` instruction, Docker runs the container process as root. If the application is compromised, the attacker has root access inside the container.
issues.suggested_fix:
Add before CMD/ENTRYPOINT:
`RUN groupadd -r appuser && useradd -r -g appuser appuser
USER appuser`
issues.after_code:
# Add near the end of your Dockerfile:
  RUN useradd -r -u 1001 -g root appuser
  USER appuser

issues.message: CORS wildcard origin (*) — any website can make credentialed requests
issues.ai_explanation: `*` as the allowed CORS origin on line 15 permits any website to read responses from your API, including with cookies/credentials if credentials are also enabled.
issues.suggested_fix: List specific allowed origins: `allowed_origins: ['https://yourapp.com', 'https://staging.yourapp.com']`

issues.message: No HEALTHCHECK instruction — container orchestrators cannot detect unhealthy state
issues.ai_explanation: Without `HEALTHCHECK`, Docker and Kubernetes cannot tell if the container is actually serving traffic. A locked-up process won't be restarted automatically.
issues.suggested_fix: Add: `HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s CMD curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1`

issues.message: Missing 'set -u' — unset variables silently expand to empty string
issues.ai_explanation: Without `set -u`, referencing an unset variable produces an empty string instead of an error. This can cause commands like `rm -rf $DIR/*` to become catastrophically destructive.
issues.suggested_fix: Add `set -u` (or `set -euo pipefail`) near the top of the script.

issues.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML — XSS risk if HTML comes from user data
issues.ai_explanation: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on line 352 bypasses React's XSS protection by directly setting raw HTML. If the `__html` value includes user content, attackers can inject malicious scripts.
issues.suggested_fix:
Sanitize with DOMPurify: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(content) }}`
Or render user content as plain text via JSX children.

issues.message: Database URL contains embedded credentials — sensitive value in config
issues.ai_explanation: The connection string on line 11 includes a username and password embedded in the URL. These are committed to source control and visible to all contributors.
issues.suggested_fix: Use separate env vars: `DB_HOST`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASS` — or load the full URL from `process.env.DATABASE_URL` / the platform's secret manager.
